_comment: GLM dev-drainer settings (issue #3688, ADR-0032 invariant 8 — the input-side half of the two-layer secret fence). Handed to the drainer's `claude` process via `--settings` by src/glm/drainer-runner.ts buildDrainerArgs(). z.ai offers no training opt-out (ADR-0032 accepted risk), so credential material must never enter the drainer's context in the first place.

HOW THE FENCE ACTUALLY WORKS. The drainer runs headless (`claude -p`) and deliberately NOT under --dangerously-skip-permissions, so a tool call matching no `allow` rule cannot fall back to an interactive prompt — it is refused. `allow` is therefore the fence, and it is deny-by-default. `deny` is evaluated before `allow`, so the Read(...) rules below additionally hard-block those paths for the path-taking tools.

WHAT THIS FILE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: deny-list Bash commands. A Read(...) deny rule constrains the Read tool ONLY — it has no effect on the Bash tool — and a Bash deny-list of file-reading primitives is unwinnable: `less`, `head`, `sed -n p`, `xxd`, `strings`, `base64`, `dd`, `grep '' .env`, `python3 -c "open(...).read()"` all reach the same bytes. A partial list reads as a fence that is not one. That exact mistake shipped in the first draft of this file — a bare `Bash` grant plus four `Bash(...)` deny prefixes, justified on the theory that the Read(...) rules fenced the Bash tool too — and was caught in QA on PR #3701. Bash is instead granted as an explicit, scoped command allow-list: the git / npm / gh / navigation verbs the authoring lane actually needs, with no shell, no interpreter, no generic file-read primitive, no `npx`, and no `gh api` / `gh secret`.

`gh pr create` is deliberately NOT granted. The drainer loop (#3689) opens the PR itself, AFTER preflightBeforePr() clears the diff — so the authoring session cannot route around the output-side gate.

RESIDUAL, stated plainly: `npm test` / `npm run *` execute repo-defined scripts, so this is a scoped-capability fence, not a sandbox. It stops incidental credential ingestion — the invariant-8 threat — not a determined exfiltration. The output-side half (preflightBeforePr's secret-scan + Verifier-Core/T4 diff gate) and the unchanged qa_orch + CI merge gate stay load-bearing.
